question.:question/problem: Consider the triangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(0,0),(1,0)$ and $(1,2),$ traversed counterclockwise, and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ Express ${∮}_{C}x{y}^{2}\,dx+2{x}^{2}y\,dy$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/2e/2e63a57e50b60d7f0c6a3ce12d164716e2cba71c6bd4c6df10460a35beba4209.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=x{y}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)=2{x}^{2}y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2xy,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=4xy.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 1,0\le y\le 2x\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}x{y}^{2}\,dx+2{x}^{2}y\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(4xy-2xy)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}2xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the square $C$ in the plane with vertices $(-1,0),(2,0),(2,3)$ and $(-1,3),$ traversed counterclockwise, and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ Express ${∮}_{C}F\cdot dr,$  where $F(x,y)=⟨3xy,{x}^{2}y⟩,$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/6f/6f831b2b707e63e8eb34ff5f6c1c45d0267f51001de2560834d212506b48ee41.png)

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∮}_{C}3xy\,dx+{x}^{2}y\,dy
$$

We have that $P(x,y)=3xy$ and $Q(x,y)={x}^{2}y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=3x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=2xy.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 3\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}3xy\,dx+{x}^{2}y\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2xy-3x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}x(2y-3)\text{ }dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the closed curve $C,$ which is the boundary of the region enclosed by the curves $x=y$ and $x=4y-{y}^{2}.$ Express ${∮}_{C}({e}^{y}-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,dx+(2x{e}^{y}+{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,dy$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](images/23/239867aec8cff7840667d2f4eafa9bc97d4fc5af09b684d863fef06fd8fd28ad.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={e}^{y}-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ and $Q(x,y)=2x{e}^{y}+{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}={e}^{y}+2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=2{e}^{y}+2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type II region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):y\le x\le 4y-{y}^{2},\,0\le y\le 3\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}({e}^{y}-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,dx+(2x{e}^{y}+{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2{e}^{y}+2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{e}^{y}-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{y}^{4y-{y}^{2}}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the closed curve $C,$ which is the boundary of the region enclosed by $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and the $x$-axis, for $\pi \le x\le 2\pi .$ Express ${\int }_{C}xdx-(x-y)dy$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/26/264cb888010525848f647669653d34383535dd32e6ac264927105540c3b85f9f.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=x$ and $Q(x,y)=-(x-y).$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=0,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):\pi \le x\le 2\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x\le y\le 0\}
$$

Therefore, applying the Green's Theorem we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xdx-(x-y)dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1)\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}^{0}dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the triangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(0,0),(0,-1)$ and $(1,0),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ Express ${∮}_{C}F\cdot dr,$  where $F(x,y)=⟨x\operatorname{cos}⁡y,x\operatorname{sin}⁡y⟩,$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/6d/6d4f13abad5cc193dccedee3114fbd9cbd9fb8e6b5b3ddb0d07f0ed2ed51f4ff.png)

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∮}_{C}x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,dx+x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy
$$

We have that $P(x,y)=x\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ and $Q(x,y)=x\operatorname{sin}⁡y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-x\operatorname{sin}⁡y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type II region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le y+1,\,-1\le y\le 0\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}x\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,dx+x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+x\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{y+1}(1+x)\operatorname{sin}⁡y\text{ }dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the closed curve $C,$ which is the boundary of the region enclosed by the unit circle and the coordinate axes in the first quadrant. Express ${∮}_{C}F\cdot dr,$  where $F(x,y)=⟨y\operatorname{cos}⁡x,x-{e}^{-{y}^{2}}⟩,$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](images/e4/e48034aed1f41cf1f9b30c057186879233fe05cd2ba720dcee436398a732b6ce.png)

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∮}_{C}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx+(x-{e}^{-{y}^{2}})\,dy
$$

We have that $P(x,y)=y\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $Q(x,y)=x-{e}^{-{y}^{2}}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx+(x-{e}^{-{y}^{2}})\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the triangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(0,-1),(1,0)$ and $(0,2),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ Express ${∮}_{C}F\cdot dr,$  where $F(x,y)=⟨{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x,xy-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡x⟩,$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/c2/c2e08c233cb31124234ab6e5179998a3bdc148024632c7770bdea46cd37dff83.png)

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∮}_{C}{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx+(xy-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,dy
$$

We have that $P(x,y)={y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $Q(x,y)=xy-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2y\operatorname{sin}⁡x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=y+2y\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 1,\,x-1\le y\le -2x+2\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx+(xy-2y\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(y+2y\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2y\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x-1}^{-2x+2}y\text{ }dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the triangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(-1,0),(1,0)$ and $(-1,2),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ Express ${∮}_{C}({y}^{2}-2xy)\,dx+(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2})\,dy$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/ea/eac7a442f0a794db0606b95aa722320d099f2bcc4e530fc6b62e9be889335da2.png)

 

We have that $P(x,y)={y}^{2}-2xy$ and $Q(x,y)=x\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2y-2x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡y-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1-x\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}({y}^{2}-2xy)\,dx+(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2})\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[\operatorname{sin}⁡y-2x-(2y-2x)]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y-2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y-2y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the rectangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(-2,0),(1,0),(1,1)$ and $(-2,1),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ Express ${∮}_{C}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx+(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+x{y}^{2})\,dy$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](images/a5/a5404053d83188af931c19350d5b6e42145009cf7f67b9dffcc08edc16ad3627.png)

 

We have that $P(x,y)=y\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $Q(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+x{y}^{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x+{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-2\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,dx+(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+x{y}^{2})\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+{y}^{2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Consider the closed curve $C,$ which is the boundary of the region enclosed by $y=1-{x}^{2}$ and $y=0.$ Express ${∮}_{C}({x}^{2}-y)\,dx+(2x-{y}^{2})\,dy$ as a repeated integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](images/a3/a3fe0bbc283a2eaacffad4b6be071f601781b6b77b2df0dd9b30abb22653c738.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={x}^{2}-y$ and $Q(x,y)=2x-{y}^{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-1,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,0\le y\le 1-{x}^{2}\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}({x}^{2}-y)\,dx+(2x-{y}^{2})\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2-(-1))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3\,\text{d}A \\  & =3{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
